# Career Workspace Conventions

Every skill in the career-os plugin reads and writes one shared folder, the **career workspace**. These conventions keep the files consistent so any skill or career-planning agent can rely on them, and so `scripts/validate_workspace.py` can check them.

## 1. Locating the workspace

1. If the user names a folder, use it.
2. Otherwise look for an existing folder named `career-workspace/` (in the working directory or any connected folder on the user's computer). It is identified by a `README.md` starting with `# Career Workspace`.
3. If none exists, ask once where to create it; default to `career-workspace/` in the working directory, or in a connected folder on their computer when one is available.
4. Create only the subfolders the current skill needs. Never delete or rename other skills' files.

The workspace is local markdown and never leaves the user's machine unless they move it. Don't suggest putting it in a public repo; if it lives in a git repo, suggest a private one.

## 2. Layout

```
career-workspace/
  README.md                 # index: status of every area, open questions, guidance for agents
  changelog.md              # one dated line per session, across all skills
  ground-truth/             # ground-truth-interview
    01-executive-summary.md
    02-core-psychology-values.md
    03-professional-capital.md      # includes ## Not claimed
    04-operating-manual.md
    05-whole-human.md               # sensitivity: restricted
    06-trajectory-non-negotiables.md  # sensitivity: restricted
    07-skill-gaps-development.md
    08-narrative-themes.md          # optional
  interests/                # interest-radar
    index.md                # table of every item + emerging patterns
    topics/<slug>.md
    companies/<slug>.md
    people/<slug>.md
    titles/<slug>.md
    projects/<slug>.md
  portfolio/                # portfolio-manifest
    sources.md              # every source ingested, when, and what was taken from it
    evidence-inventory.md   # atomic evidence items (EV-###)
    manifest.md             # the curated portfolio manifest
  titles/                   # title-lab
    candidates.md           # scoreboard of every title explored
    <slug>.md               # deep dive per title
    title-stack.md          # chosen title(s) + rationale
  positioning/              # positioning-studio
    positioning.md          # core positioning, angles, proof map
    experiments.md          # market tests and inbound log
    assets/<audience>.md    # bios, headlines, intros per audience/channel
    assets/story-bank.md    # interview stories built from evidence
  decisions/                # decisions the user made with the career-strategist
    journal.md
```

## 3. File rules

**Frontmatter on every file** except `README.md` and `changelog.md`:

```yaml
---
title: <human title>
type: ground-truth | interest | portfolio | title | positioning | index | decision
status: complete | partial | draft | not_started | archived
last_updated: YYYY-MM-DD
open_questions: []
# optional:
review_after: YYYY-MM-DD        # overrides the staleness default below
sensitivity: public | private | restricted
derived_from: [EV-001, EV-004]  # evidence this file's claims rest on
approved_on: YYYY-MM-DD         # when the user approved the current content
---
```

**Staleness defaults** (days since `last_updated`), used unless `review_after` is set: ground-truth 180, portfolio 180, title 180, positioning 120, interest 365, decision 90. Treat stale files as possibly out of date: confirm before relying on them.

**Slugs:** kebab-case, e.g. `companies/anthropic.md`, `titles/design-engineer.md`.

**Provenance tags** on facts that matter:
- `[stated]` the user said it in conversation
- `[source: <name or URL>]` extracted from a document or page the user supplied
- `[researched: <URL>]` found by Claude via web research (market facts only, never facts about the user)
- `[suggested]` Claude proposed it; not yet approved. Never allowed in `positioning/` or `titles/title-stack.md`.
- `[suggested → approved]` Claude proposed it and the user approved it

**Never write unapproved claims about the user.** Facts about the user come only from the user or from sources they supplied. Generated text (a bio, an earlier draft, a story) is never a source for a fact; trace every claim back to ground truth or an EV item.

**Sensitivity.** `ground-truth/05` and `06` (life context, comp, dealbreakers) default to `restricted`. Restricted content:
- never goes into web search queries or fetched URLs;
- is passed to subagents only when the task needs it (e.g., a comp floor for filtering), and then without name, gender, age, or other demographic details;
- is never quoted in outward-facing assets.

**Missing values:** `_Not yet captured_`. Never leave a heading empty.

**Cross-links:** relative links, e.g. `[Win 2](../ground-truth/03-professional-capital.md#win-2)`, or evidence IDs like `EV-014`.

**Changes over time:** when a value changes (salary floor, target title, goal), note the old value in `changelog.md` rather than keeping history inside the file.

## 4. Evidence and proof maps

- Evidence items live in `portfolio/evidence-inventory.md` as `### EV-###: <short name>`. IDs are defined once and never renumbered or reused. Any skill may append a new item (e.g., a win the user just described) using the next free number and the inventory format.
- Every outward-facing file (`positioning/positioning.md`, every `positioning/assets/*.md`) ends with a proof map:

  ```markdown
  ## Proof map
  | Claim | Evidence |
  |---|---|
  | Lifted checkout conversion 12% | EV-001 |
  | Cut onboarding time in half | [stated] 2026-10-04 |
  ```

  Every row cites an EV ID, a workspace link, or a provenance tag. Every number in the asset (percentages, money, multipliers, counts) must appear in a proof-map row, and when the row cites only EV IDs, in one of those EV items.

## 5. The "Not claimed" list

`ground-truth/03-professional-capital.md` has a `## Not claimed` section: skills, tools, credentials, titles, and scopes the user does not have or does not want to claim, one per bullet as `- <term>: <note>`. It exists because the most common fabrication is a plausible skill the person lacks. Outward-facing files must not mention these terms, except under a "Not for" or "Retired" heading.

## 6. Validation

Each skill ships `scripts/validate_workspace.py` (Python 3.9+, standard library only):

```bash
python3 <skill-dir>/scripts/validate_workspace.py <path-to-career-workspace>
python3 <skill-dir>/scripts/validate_workspace.py <path-to-career-workspace> --stale   # also list open questions
```

Run it at the end of every session (and after any big write), fix every ERROR, and run it again until clean. If Python isn't available, check the same rules by hand. In Claude Code, a plugin hook also runs it after each write to a workspace file and reports errors immediately.

| Code | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| E-FM | Frontmatter missing or invalid | Add or correct the keys above |
| E-EV-DUP | An EV ID defined twice | Give the new item the next free ID |
| E-EV-REF | An EV ID cited but not defined | Cite the right ID, or add the evidence with the user |
| E-UNAPPROVED | Bare `[suggested]` in an outward file | Get approval, or remove it |
| E-PROOF-MAP | Asset without a proof map, or a row without evidence | Add the map; trace the claim or drop it |
| E-NUMBER | A number not traceable to evidence | Trace it, ask the user, or remove it |
| E-ABSENCE | An outward file mentions a "Not claimed" term | Remove it |
| E-CHANGELOG | Files changed today but no changelog line | Append the line |

**Never fix a finding by inventing evidence.** If a claim can't be traced, ask the user or remove it.

## 7. README.md and changelog.md

Each skill updates its own row and adds to the open questions. Create the README if missing:

```markdown
# Career Workspace: <Name>

Living source of truth for career planning. Everything about <Name> here was stated, supplied, or approved by them. Stored locally.

## How agents should use this
- Treat `ground-truth/` as authoritative. Hard dealbreakers and financial minimums are filters.
- Anti-skills mean "capable but unwilling": never recommend roles built around them. `## Not claimed` items are never attributed to them.
- `interests/` shows pull (what attracts them); `portfolio/` shows proof (what they've done). Recommendations should sit where pull and proof overlap.
- `titles/title-stack.md` and `positioning/positioning.md` are the approved way to describe them. Reuse that language.
- `_Not yet captured_` and open questions are unknowns: ask, don't guess.
- Files past their staleness window (see `review_after` or the defaults) may be out of date.
- Files marked `sensitivity: restricted` stay out of web searches and outward-facing text.

## Status
| Area | Location | Status | Last updated |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ground truth | ground-truth/ | not_started | |
| Interests | interests/ | not_started | |
| Portfolio | portfolio/ | not_started | |
| Titles | titles/ | not_started | |
| Positioning | positioning/ | not_started | |
| Decisions | decisions/ | not_started | |

## Open questions
```

`changelog.md`: append one line per session: `- YYYY-MM-DD [skill-name]: <what was created/updated>; <notable changes, including old → new values>`.

## 8. Coaching rules (all skills)

- **Assess first, honestly.** When the user asks for a judgment, give it before any encouragement. Name weak spots plainly.
- **Hold evidence-based judgments under pushback.** If the user disagrees, restate the evidence. Change the assessment only for new evidence or a preference you hadn't captured, and say which it was.
- **No demographic reasoning.** Compensation and fit guidance come only from cited market data (`[researched: ...]`) and the user's stated numbers and preferences, never from name, gender, age, ethnicity, or nationality.
- **Push past generic answers once**, then accept what the user gives.
- **Suggest, label, and wait.** Proposed phrasings are `[suggested]` until the user approves them.

## 9. Session etiquette

- Read `README.md` first and any files the skill depends on, so you never ask for something already captured.
- Keep your own turns short; ask 2–4 questions at a time.
- Save as you go, not only at the end.
- Close by running the validator until clean, updating the README status row and the changelog, then suggesting the most useful next skill based on what's still missing.
